## What it is

IT-Tools is one web page with about a hundred small helpers for developers and admins: UUID and password generators, JSON and YAML converters, JWT and certificate decoders, subnet calculators, QR codes and more ([CorentinTh/it-tools](https://github.com/CorentinTh/it-tools)). It is part of the Supply Depot (issue #129, NMD-04).

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L2** (copyleft). OneMind only runs upstream's unmodified image as a separate program; no IT-Tools code is copied into OneMind's Apache-2.0 code, which is what keeps the two licences apart. There is no research licence-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment`, one container: upstream's image `docker.io/corentinth/it-tools`, which is the stock `nginx:stable-alpine` (nginx 1.26.2) with the built web page.
- **Why it can run locked down:** every tool runs in your browser, so the server only hands out static files and stores nothing. The image itself sets no `USER` (it would start as root), so the pod runs nginx as the image's own unprivileged `nginx` user (UID 101) instead, the same pattern as `apps/excalidraw`.
- Read-only root filesystem with small scratch volumes (`/var/cache/nginx`, `/run`, `/tmp`). The namespaced "safe" sysctl `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0` lets the non-root nginx bind port 80 inside this pod only. RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, no service-account token.
- Probes: `GET /`.
- Image pinned by tag and digest, read from the Docker Hub registry API on 2026-11-19; the index has amd64 and arm64. Its nginx and Alpine base are from 2024, so the CI scan may find fixed CVEs; if it finds a CRITICAL with a fix, the gate blocks the app and the reason is written below.

## First run

Source: [IT-Tools README](https://github.com/CorentinTh/it-tools#readme).

1. Install IT-Tools from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-it-tools`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-it-tools port-forward svc/it-tools 8080:8080
   ```
3. Pick a tool from the list or the search box.
